Question B-006-002-009.

Why the correct answer is right: A balanced transmission line uses two parallel conductors carrying equal and opposite RF currents. Neither conductor is intended to be the grounded shield around the other.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "has one conductor inside the other": One conductor inside another describes coaxial cable, which is normally unbalanced.
- sourceIndex 2: "carries RF current on one wire only": RF current needs a return path; a one-wire-only description leaves out the equal opposite current of a balanced line.
- sourceIndex 3: "is made of one conductor only": A single conductor is not a complete transmission line for carrying RF energy between source and load.
